facts.label: What METU accepts for admission

value.text: A national exam or diploma score can be used if it meets METU's minimum; otherwise an exam such as the SAT. A level applicants whose results come after the deadline receive an admission deferral and are decided when final results arrive in August.

facts.where: Before Application, and the note to A level applicants on the dates page

facts.label: Minimum requirement for Bangladeshi applicants (METU)

value.text: At least 90% success in a school-leaving certificate that allows entry to a 4-year undergraduate programme. Meeting the minimum does not guarantee admission.

facts.note: METU's sheet was last updated on 5 January 2024. It does not say how an HSC GPA out of 5 converts to a percentage, so the plan shows the rule as written.

facts.label: Turkish student visa: documents (Embassy in Dhaka)

value.text: Apply only after enrolling. The visa is single-entry and generally valid for six months. Needed: a passport valid for one year, two photographs, the acceptance letter emailed by the university to the embassy, a copy of the diploma attested by Bangladesh's Ministry of Education and Ministry of Foreign Affairs, exam results if taken, a medical certificate from a recognised hospital including an HIV test, travel insurance, and one year of bank statements with a solvency certificate. All documents in English.

facts.where: Information regarding education visa, items 1 to 8
facts.note: The embassy's education visa page is dated 25 June 2019 and is still its newest. Mosaic Visa's 2026 lists also ask for 3 biometric photos, a copy of your national ID or birth certificate, and travel health insurance bought through Mosaic. Confirm the list with Mosaic Visa.

facts.label: Turkish student visa from Bangladesh

value.text: Applications are by appointment only, booked on Mosaic Visa's website.

facts.note: Mosaic Visa is the centre named by the embassy. It lists no separate fee or document list for student visas, so confirm both with Mosaic.

facts.label: Turkish student visa processing time
facts.note: Mosaic Visa says processing may take up to 45 days, and that a submitted application cannot be withdrawn until a decision is made. The plan uses the full 45. Kept as one published figure, not as observed waits.

facts.label: Length of a bachelor's degree in Türkiye

value.text: At least eight semesters, four years and 240 ECTS credits. Some programmes take five or six years. A foreign-language preparatory year, of up to two years, does not count towards this.

facts.where: Sections on programme length and the preparatory class

value.text: At state universities, the lowest and highest yearly fees for students admitted from abroad are set by presidential decision. Foundation universities set their own fees.

facts.note: The principles are in Turkish; this is a translation of the fee rule.

facts.label: Turkish universities in the QS World University Rankings 2027

value.text: 25 universities from Türkiye are in the QS World University Rankings 2027, 6 of them in the top 500 and 11 in the top 1,000.

facts.label: Türkiye Bursları: monthly stipend for undergraduates
facts.note: The page gives no date for this amount. Merit scholars receive twice the regular stipend. METU estimates basic living costs in Ankara at 8,000 to 15,000 TL a month without housing, so the stipend may not cover everyday costs.

facts.label: Türkiye Bursları: number of programme choices

value.text: Applicants can choose up to 12 different programmes and universities, and are placed in one of them.

facts.note: From YTB's 2025 guide page; placement among the 12 choices is from YTB's archived guide. Checked again when the 2027 call opens.

facts.label: Türkiye Bursları: how scholars are selected

value.text: Applications are checked against the basic criteria, then reviewed by expert committees, which choose who goes forward. Shortlisted undergraduate applicants take a 60-minute, 30-question test of mathematics, geometry and logic, and a face-to-face interview on the same day.

facts.note: The page does not say where interviews for Bangladesh are held. Expect to attend in person.

value.text: Applications from 10 January to 20 February, evaluation in March and April, interviews from April to June, results in early August, and travel to Türkiye in September.
Applications are free of charge, through the Türkiye Scholarships Information System.

facts.label: Türkiye Bursları: applying through agents

value.text: There are no institutions or persons authorised to apply for Türkiye Scholarships. Applications can only be made by the candidates themselves, on turkiyeburslari.gov.tr.

facts.note: From YTB's archived applicant guide, which carries no date.

facts.label: Türkiye Bursları: language of study

value.text: Applicants can see each programme's language of instruction while choosing. Most programmes are taught in Turkish, and every scholar without a C1 Turkish certificate attends a one-year Turkish course and must reach C1, even when placed in an English-taught programme.

facts.note: The current application steps page also says the language is shown in the system. The Turkish course rule comes from the archived guide.

facts.label: Türkiye Bursları: documents for the online application

value.text: A valid passport or ID, a recent photo, national exam results if any, a diploma or temporary graduation certificate, a transcript, and any test or language certificate your chosen programmes require.

facts.label: Türkiye Bursları: Merit Scholarship for undergraduates

value.text: For outstanding students. You need an average of at least 90%, and also one of these: an SAT of 1400 with 680 in Math for engineering or 1350 for other subjects (or IB 33), together with TOEFL iBT 80 or IELTS 6.5; a top-10 rank in your country's national exam; or a medal at an international science olympiad. It pays twice the regular stipend.

facts.label: Applying before your school results are out (METU)

value.text: If your diploma is also your exam result, you must wait for the result in order to apply, and applications after the deadline are not accepted. METU recommends applying with an SAT score instead.

facts.where: Answer on applicants who have not graduated yet
facts.note: The HSC is a diploma of this kind.

facts.label: Applying with expected A level results (METU)

value.text: Applicants can apply with expected A level results and are conditionally accepted until the results arrive.

facts.where: Answer on expected A level results

facts.label: SAT and A level minimums (METU)

value.text: An SAT total of at least 1200, with at least 700 in Math for engineering, architecture and science programmes. A levels: ABB in three subjects, two of them relevant to the programme. IB: 33.

facts.note: From METU's sheet last updated on 5 January 2024.

facts.label: English requirement (METU)

value.text: To start the degree without the English preparatory year: METU's own exam at 60, TOEFL iBT 75 or PTE Academic 65, with scores valid for two years. IELTS taken on or after 24 December 2022 is not accepted. An English score is not needed to apply.

facts.note: The IELTS rule and the optional score are on METU's English proficiency page for international applicants.

facts.label: Admission rules for international applicants (Bilkent)

value.text: Applications for autumn 2026 ran from 2 February to 12 July 2026, and applications with predicted grades or results are not evaluated. HSC: at least 80%, in the stream related to the programme. A levels: three, each at least C, at least one related to the programme. IB: 28.

facts.note: The HSC, A level and IB minimums are in Bilkent's minimum scores sheet, which is undated and still names SAT Subject Tests, so confirm the HSC and SAT rules with Bilkent.

values.note: Including 10% VAT, paid in two halves. The fee has risen for each new intake: 17,600 USD for 2025 and 18,400 USD for 2026.

value.text: Tuition waivers at five levels, from 20% to 100%, for applicants who ask for financial assistance, judged on their school grades. A limited number of top students with a full waiver also receive housing. Keeping a waiver needs a yearly average of at least 2.00 out of 4.
IELTS 6.5 with at least 5.5 in each section, or TOEFL iBT 87, valid at registration.

facts.label: Tuition fee per year for international students (Koç)

value.text: For international students admitted in autumn 2025: 38,000 USD a year for every programme except medicine, and 59,000 USD for medicine.

facts.note: No figure for students starting in 2026 or 2027 was published on 21 October 2026.

value.text: Merit scholarships cover full or partial tuition only. Every applicant is considered, and no test score or grade guarantees a scholarship.

facts.label: National certificates accepted (Koç)

value.text: Bangladesh's HSC is not on Koç's list of accepted national qualifications. Koç accepts international exams instead, including the SAT, ACT, A levels, IB and TR-YÖS (at least 425 out of 500, higher for engineering, computer science and business). The SAT minimum is 1200 to 1450, depending on the school.

facts.note: The page still shows 2024 dates, so check it with Koç.

facts.label: Exams and certificates accepted (Sabancı)

value.text: HSC: an average of at least 80%. SAT 1100, which is not mandatory and cannot be a superscore; ACT 23; two A levels at C; IB 28; TR-YÖS 350. Final-year students may apply, and applicants hear about their evaluation by email within two to three weeks.

facts.note: The final-year rule and the timing are on Sabancı's application requirements page. Sabancı works out the percentage as the total of your marks divided by the number of subjects. Ask Sabancı how it treats an HSC GPA out of 5.

facts.label: Scholarships (Sabancı)

value.text: Admission scholarships waive part or all of the tuition, are given without a separate application, and are limited in number, with priority for early applicants. They cover tuition only, a separate dormitory scholarship covers housing, and no score guarantees a percentage.

facts.note: Limited numbers and early priority are on Sabancı's scholarships page.

facts.label: International applications for 2026 to 2027 (Istanbul Technical University)

value.text: A second round of international applications ran from 21 to 26 August 2026, with results on 1 September. Final-year school students may apply with an official document showing their expected graduation date.

facts.where: Application dates and who may apply
facts.note: ITU's first-round page for 2026 has been taken down.

facts.label: Exams accepted for admission (Istanbul Technical University)

value.text: SAT 1200 with 650 in Math, ACT 26, A levels with an A in maths or physics and two more at C or above, IB 30, or TR-YÖS 400. Bangladesh's HSC is not on the list, and only the listed exams are accepted.

facts.note: The rule that only listed exams are accepted is on ITU's 2026 to 2027 application announcement.

facts.label: Tuition for international students, 2026 to 2027 (Istanbul Technical University)

value.text: For students who started between autumn 2023 and autumn 2026: 94,500 a year in the engineering faculties, 86,500 in management, 79,000 in arts and sciences, and 119,000 in naval architecture, maritime and textiles, paid in two halves. The page does not name the currency.

facts.note: Ask Istanbul Technical University which currency applies before you plan.

facts.label: English requirement (Istanbul Technical University)

value.text: TOEFL iBT 4 on the new scale (72 before 21 January 2026), PTE Academic 59, or ITU's own exam at 60, valid for two years. IELTS is not on the list.

facts.note: ITU says TOEFL iBT and PTE results must come from test centres at state universities. Ask ITU whether a test taken in Bangladesh is accepted before you book.

facts.label: TR-YÖS, the entrance exam for students from abroad

value.text: Run by ÖSYM, Türkiye's national testing centre, with a centre in Dhaka. It has 40 numerical aptitude and 40 basic mathematics questions in 100 minutes, is scored from 100 to 500, and is valid for two years from the exam date. Each university sets which exams it accepts, so check its list.

facts.where: Sections on exam centres, content, validity and use

facts.label: TR-YÖS sessions in 2026

value.text: TR-YÖS/1 on 12 April 2026, with applications from 14 January to 3 February and late applications to 11 February. TR-YÖS/2 on 11 October 2026, with applications from 9 July to 3 August and late applications from 7 to 11 August.

facts.note: The first session's dates are in ÖSYM's TR-YÖS/1 guide. Dates for 2027 were not yet published on 21 October 2026.

facts.label: TR-YÖS fee for the Dhaka centre (October 2026 sitting)
facts.note: 1,100 TL for the April 2026 sitting and 1,150 TL for October 2026. The fee usually rises with each sitting.

facts.label: Where Bangladeshi applicants apply for a Turkish visa

value.text: Since 1 February 2026, only Mosaic Visa accepts Turkish visa applications in Bangladesh, at House 77, Block M, Road 11, Banani, Dhaka.

facts.label: Whose bank statements count for a Turkish visa

value.text: Only bank statements of the applicant, the applicant's parents or the applicant's spouse are accepted.

facts.label: The e-Visa and study

value.text: Holders of ordinary Bangladeshi passports need a visa. The e-Visa is only for tourism or business, so students need a student visa.

facts.where: Rules for Bangladesh and for the e-Visa

facts.label: The equivalency certificate for your school certificate

value.text: Universities need an equivalency certificate for your school-leaving certificate, issued by Türkiye's Ministry of National Education, through its e-Denklik system, or by a Turkish mission abroad.

facts.note: From Ondokuz Mayıs University's page. Üsküdar University advises getting it in your home country before you travel, says registration is cancelled if it is not delivered on time, and asks for an apostilled diploma. Ask your university whether it needs an apostille or the ministry attestation used for the visa.

facts.label: Student residence permit

value.text: Apply online on e-ikamet before your visa expires, then hand in your documents as your university tells you. Health insurance that covers the whole permit period is compulsory. Students pay only the card fee, not a permit fee.

facts.note: The insurance rule is on the Migration Management e-ikamet page. Istanbul Technical University's page gives the same timing rule.

facts.label: Residence permit card fee for students in 2026
facts.note: Students pay no visa fee or residence permit fee, only this card fee.

facts.label: State health insurance for international students

value.text: International students can join Türkiye's general health insurance (GSS) only if they apply within three months of the start of the academic year. With GSS, the residence permit can be issued for the whole study period; with private insurance, only for the period it covers.

facts.where: Note on general health insurance for students
facts.note: Universities count the three months from slightly different days: METU from the first day of autumn classes, Ankara University from first enrolment, so follow the earliest date your university gives. Ankara University says a student who misses it cannot join at any point during their studies. The rule on the permit period is on Istanbul Technical University's residence permit page.

facts.label: General health insurance for a student, per month in 2026
facts.note: METU gives about 1,300 TL a month for 2026, about 15,600 TL a year. The amount follows the minimum wage, so it changes every year.

value.text: Appointments on e-ikamet are free. Do not pay anyone to book them.

facts.label: Working while you study in Türkiye

value.text: Bachelor's students can get a work permit only after completing their first year, for part-time jobs off campus. The employer applies for the permit, and a residence permit alone does not give the right to work.

facts.note: From METU's page. The law itself (International Labour Force Law, Article 19) could not be read automatically.

facts.label: Türkiye Bursları: Success Scholarship for students already in Türkiye

value.text: YTB's calendar lists a Success Scholarship, with applications in October and November. It is for international students already studying in Türkiye who have completed at least a year there and hold no other scholarship.

facts.note: The calendar gives the months. The conditions come from YTB's archived guide, so check them when you apply.

facts.label: Rules at Mosaic Visa

value.text: Applicants attend in person for biometrics, pay in cash in taka at the centre, and apply no more than 90 days before they travel. Mosaic asks for 3 biometric photos, a copy of a national ID card or birth certificate, and travel health insurance bought through Mosaic.

facts.note: These are Mosaic's general visa rules; it publishes no separate list for students.

facts.label: General visa fee at Mosaic Visa, six months, single entry

value.text: 28,730 taka for a single-entry visa valid for six months, plus service charges. Mosaic lists no separate fee for student visas.

facts.note: Ask Mosaic Visa for the student visa fee before you go.
